what_it_does: In analog and mixed-signal (AMS) chip design — circuits that handle real-world continuous signals like radio waves or sensor readings alongside digital logic — an important accuracy problem is predicting 'parasitic capacitance': tiny unintended electrical capacitances that form between wires and components because of their physical proximity on the chip, which slow down signals and waste power. Training a machine-learning model to predict these values normally requires huge labeled datasets of real chip measurements, which are expensive and scarce. CircuitGPS reframes the problem as a graph: circuit components are nodes and potential parasitic couplings between them are edges, forming a complex network. It pre-trains a graph neural network (a type of model designed to learn patterns in networks) on the simpler task of predicting whether a coupling exists at all (link prediction), then fine-tunes it on the harder task of predicting how large each coupling is (edge regression), making effective use of the limited labeled data available.
